historical_references.reference: Callum was derived from the Scottish and Old Celtic name, Colin or Calum, meaning 'young dog'. It was popularized as a Christian given name during the Middle Ages when the Scottish people converted to Christianity.

Callum was also used as a variant of the Irish name, Colum, which means 'dove'. This name was borne by several prominent Irish saints, including St. Colum Cille (Columba) of Iona and St. Callistus (Colum) of Ardfert.
